texts.orig: Proposition 2.13 . Let F be a positive integral ∆n -frieze and fix an i ∈ { 1, . . . , n } . There is a ∆n -frieze F ′ corresponding to ( x1, . . . , xn ; y1, . . . , yn ) ∈ X∆ n ( N 2n ) such that F is a horizontal translation of F ′ and xi ≤ bi,∆ n . Furthermore, if all entries in F are at least 2 , then xi ≤ ci,∆ n .
texts.text: Proposition 2.13 . Let F be a positive integral ∆n -frieze and fix an i ∈ { 1, . . . , n } . There is a ∆n -frieze F ′ corresponding to ( x1, . . . , xn ; y1, . . . , yn ) ∈ X∆ n ( N 2n ) such that F is a horizontal translation of F ′ and xi ≤ bi,∆ n . Furthermore, if all entries in F are at least 2 , then xi ≤ ci,∆ n .

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Proof. Each ∆n -frieze F is a horizontal translation of a frieze F ′ in its Z /P∆ n Z -orbit such that F ′ i,1 ≤ F ′ i,j for all 1 ≤ j ≤ P∆ n . By Lemma 2.11, there is a bound on ∏ P ∆n j = 1 F ′ i,j ≤ b P ∆n i,∆ n . But xi = F ′ i,1 is the smallest factor in the product of P∆ n -many terms, hence xi ≤ bi,∆ n . If the entries of F are all at least 2 , then the entries of the translation F ′ are also all at least 2 . Hence the same argument gives the bound in terms of ci,∆ n instead of bi,∆ n . □
